This app: the HUD, the voice announcer, the rules and the settings.
Reads the radio's channels and telemetry. Its libraries are included in the app. Thank you, RadioMaster, for publishing it.
The Qt libraries that come with the RadioMaster SDK, as delivered with it. Source code: download.qt.io.
The C++ runtime of the Android NDK, needed by the SDK.
The standard library of the Kotlin language, which the app is written in.
Welcome to AX-HUD
AX-HUD shows the video from the HDMI input of your AX12 full screen, with a HUD on top, and speaks announcements and warnings. It only reads from the radio and never writes to it. This guide takes about a minute.
Allow the camera
The HDMI input reaches Android as a camera, so AX-HUD needs the camera permission. If you said no by mistake, allow it in the Android settings, under Apps, AX-HUD, Permissions. Without it you see the gray No video screen.
The first data takes about 12 seconds
After you open the app, the radio data (sticks, link quality, telemetry) appears after about 12 seconds. That wait is inside the RadioMaster SDK and is not an error. A banner counts the seconds. The video starts at once.
Where everything is
Tap MENU at the top right for six tiles: Sound rules, Speech, Battery, Aircraft, Settings and Exit. Choose your aircraft and battery pack first, because their limits drive the warnings. Settings holds the overlays, the layout, the checks, the languages and the updates.
An aid, not a safety system
AX-HUD helps you see and hear what your aircraft is doing. Do not rely on it as your only warning. Always fly within your local rules.
Drag a card to move it. Drag the square handle to resize it. Tap Done when you are finished.

Arm switch channel (1 to 16, AUX1 is channel 5)
Counts as armed at or above (microseconds)
Counts as disarmed below (microseconds)
The gap between the two thresholds stops a bump of the switch from arming or disarming the statistics. The switch must stay put for 0.3 seconds.

Current limit line (amps)
Height comes from the GPS altitude relative to where you armed, so expect a few meters of error. The bar turns red when the current is above the limit line.
Flight statistics rows
The current limit is 5 to 300 amps
Left of the sticks
Right of the sticks
On      Channel      Name on the overlay                 Reverse
A bar fills with the channel value. Gray-blue = low, amber = middle, green = high. Names are written along the bar; a short name reads best.\n\nReverse: tick it for a switch that is reversed in the radio, so the bar shows the switch the way you flip it (up = full and green). Only the picture changes: sound and warning rules still use the real channel values.
Channel bars
Defaults
Bar {0}: the channel must be 1 to 16
Mode 1: left = pitch + yaw, right = throttle + roll
Mode 2: left = throttle + yaw, right = pitch + roll
Mode 3: left = throttle + roll, right = pitch + yaw
Mode 4: left = pitch + roll, right = throttle + yaw

Left stick up/down drawn reversed
Left stick left/right drawn reversed
Right stick up/down drawn reversed
Right stick left/right drawn reversed
The sticks show the channel values the radio sends. Common order: roll 1, pitch 2, throttle 3, yaw 4. Turn a direction round if the dot moves the wrong way.

Exit AX-HUD?
The radio link stops and the radio's serial port is released. There is no HUD and no voice until you start the app again.

Text editor
Each check shows a tick when its condition is true and a cross when not, before you arm. The switch on the left turns a check off without deleting it.
A warning shows in the status bar while its condition is true. Critical = red and blinking, warning = amber, info = blue. The switch on the left turns a rule off without deleting it.
A rule speaks when its condition becomes true. The switch on the left turns a rule off without deleting it.
Speech is muted (MENU, Speech)
$low  - warning limit of the active battery profile
$crit  - critical limit
$full  - limit for a full pack

Language
Speech language
The screen and the voice can use different languages. Your rules keep their own words: "Reset the rules to the defaults" loads the starting rules in the voice's language.
Display
Always show the MENU button
Off: the button hides and appears when you touch the screen.

Aircraft and battery
Active aircraft
Manage the aircraft (add, rename, delete)...
Each aircraft keeps its own rules, warning rules, checks, battery profiles and packs, channel bars, stick mapping and arm switch. Overlay looks, language and updates are shared.
Active battery profile
Edit the packs of this aircraft...
Edit the battery profiles (cells and voltage limits)...
Rules and checks can use the value cell (volts per cell) and the limits $low, $crit and $full of the active profile, for example: cell < $low -> battery low. Switching the profile changes the numbers, not the rules.

Drag a card to move it and drag its square handle to resize it. Cards that are switched off are not shown. The Size setting of a card is its starting size; resizing multiplies it.

Updates
Check for updates now
Update channel
Check at start-up (needs internet)
Android asks you to confirm every update. The first time it also asks you to allow installs from AX-HUD. Never update during a flight.
Diagnostics
Show the variables panel (every value the radio sends)
Test channels: sliders instead of the radio
Show the start-up timings of the last launches...
The radio link starts on a background thread and keeps running while the app's own screens, file pickers and rebuilds come and go; it stops when you leave the app. The SDK itself needs about 12 seconds to open the radio's serial port; the timings show where the time goes.
Close Settings to see the panels over the video.
